correctness.rationale: The graph consists of K5 on {u,v,a,b,c} plus x,y adjacent to both u,v; it has 7 vertices,14 edges and beta1=8. The ordered deleted-product CW model for F(G,2) was independently built with 42 zero-,140 one-,82 two-cells; exact rational boundary ranks 41 and77, and d1*d2=0 in every column. Thus H1 dimension=140-41-77=22. For finite connected G not homeomorphic to a circle, Barnett–Farber Proposition 1.3/2.3 gives surjectivity of inclusion-induced H1 into H1(GxG) of rank 2 beta1=16, hence kernel dimension 6. Removing uv and deleting endpoints leaves components K3, {x}, {y}; Farber–Hanbury Theorem14 yields a lower bound of 2*3-2=4 for the same kernel, so 6 is strictly greater. Computation is exact over Q (no modular inference) and has a complete cell list; no claim about Z torsion.
residual_risks: Correctness of dimension6 relies on published surjectivity of inclusion on H1 for connected noncircle graphs; that theorem is applicable here. No integral torsion or general 2-cut formula is asserted.

evidence: Theorem14 supplies a free subgroup of rank 4 after adding the uv edge across three components, not equality. General mature graph results ensure certain kernels vanish, inapplicable here because there is a two-cut.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The actual 6-dimensional exact kernel strictly exceeds the 4 lower bound, so that bound does not imply the result. Complete/bipartite graph formulae apply to K5 or K_{m,n}, not to the present hybrid graph; no covering explicit family theorem was identified.

value.rationale: A canonical nonplanar 2-cut stress test (a K5 block with two twin length-two attachments at the same pair) demonstrates that the standard two-cut lower bound of 4 need not be exact: the actual kernel dimension is 6. This supplies a reproducible, integral-chain-defined rational test case for refining intersection-form rank estimates, not an arbitrary floating-point number or rebranding of the published lower bound. It is deliberately a narrow but nontrivial structural benchmark, not a general classification.
